title: Flood Inundation Mapping Working Group
description: Cultivates a vibrant Community of Practice among CIROH researchers and federal partners, providing thought leadership by synthesizing CIROH's advancements in FIM and aligning them with broader developments in the FIM research community. Serves as a key advocate for FIM within CIROH, informing strategic direction and CIROH roadmap development.

objectives: Analyze CIROH's research portfolio and the broader research community FIM research. Provide input for roadmaps, governance documents, and documentation for CIROH's community FIM products.
Develop a scholarly product (e.g., journal article, special issue in a high-profile journal, conference session) spotlighting CIROH's research advances in large-domain FIM.
Initiate discussions with the CIROH R2X team and OWP personnel toward the development of a FIM-centric R2O transition roadmap.
Support FIM-related education and training opportunities, including webinars, DevCon workshops, hackathons, and Summer Institute participation.
accomplishments: Monthly virtual meeting, and two in-person meetings (during DevCon26 and Science Meeting)
Six (6) seminar presentations by group members (Objective #4)
Two (2) presentations by OWP staff on research efforts and operational tools (Objectives #4 & #3)
Identification of six (6) training workshops for the FIM track in the 2026 CIROH Developers Conference (Objective #4)
Development of a large overview paper involving over a dozen WG members (Objective #2)

title: Decision Support Working Group
description: Focuses on understanding and advancing CIROH's decision support and social and behavioral sciences research portfolio, providing strategic guidance and visibility for these critical research areas.

objectives: Develop recommendations to guide CIROH's integration of decision support and social and behavioral science across research activities.
Lead the development of a journal article synthesizing CIROH's decision support and social science research-to-impact advances.

Organize activities that increase the visibility of CIROH's decision support portfolio, such as lead/co-lead conference sessions, serve on steering committees, or otherwise contribute to activities supporting CIROH's priorities.

title: Hydrologic Modeling and Prediction Working Group
description: Aligns and synthesizes CIROH's hydrologic modeling research advances with those from the hydrologic sciences community. Informs CIROH's hydrologic modeling strategy and roadmap while organizing activities to advance the state of CIROH's hydrologic modeling research.

objectives: Lead the development of a thought piece, journal article, and/or conference presentation providing a vision for hydrologic modeling and prediction that informs CIROH's hydrologic modeling research.

Analyze CIROH's research portfolio and broader hydrologic sciences community hydrologic modeling research and inform CIROH's medium and long-term hydrologic modeling research and development strategy and roadmap.
Contribute to the creation of a CIROH-sponsored cross-institution large-domain hydrologic modeling course.

title: Hydroinformatics Working Group
description: Connects CIROH researchers, federal partners, and the broader water data science community who build the data, software, and cyberinfrastructure that carry research into operations. The WG helps synthesize CIROH's hydroinformatics advances with those made by the wider community and informs how they are organized and shared through the CIROH Hub. It promotes standards, interoperability, and good practice for sharing data, code, and models, and it coordinates cross-institutional projects so teams build on each other's work. The WG also organizes training, including Developers Conference workshops and a proposed hydroinformatics field camp, with an emphasis on students and early-career scientists.

objectives: Synthesize and coordinate cross-institutional research proposals and projects, connecting teams that work on similar hydroinformatics problems.
Improve, integrate, and document the CIROH Hub (which merged the CIROH Portal and DocuHub) so CIROH data, applications, notebooks, and publications are easy to find, use, and contribute to.
Systematically evaluate how CIROH research shares data and code, and recommend best practices for data management and sharing.
Develop a scholarly product highlighting CIROH's research advances in hydroinformatics.
Support hydroinformatics education and training, including Developers Conference workshops, webinars, and planning for a hydroinformatics field camp.
accomplishments: Virtual kickoff meeting (September 2025) and WG meetup (July 2026), an in-person breakout and WG dinner at the 2025 CIROH Science Meeting, and an October 2026 coordination meeting on upcoming events, workshops, and trainings
Coordinated fifteen (15) FY26 white papers across ten (10) institutions, with four (4) invited to full proposals, including HydroServer as a core community data service (Objective #1)
Helped design and launch the CIROH Hub (hub.ciroh.org) in February 2026, merging the CIROH Portal and DocuHub, with more than 17 design recommendations from WG members (Objective #2)
Audit of data and code sharing across 299 CIROH-funded publications, in partnership with CUAHSI, with a paper now under review at AGU Earth and Space Science (Objective #3)

Review paper "Bridging the Research-to-Operations Gaps in NOAA Water Prediction through Advances in Hydroinformatics," with eleven (11) authors from eight (8) institutions, in press in the Journal of the American Water Resources Association (Objective #4)
Hydroinformatics and Data Science track at the 2025 and 2026 CIROH Developers Conferences, led by WG members (Objective #5)
Developed CIROH's data sharing guiding principles and best-practice recommendations for sharing data, code, and models (2023-2024, as Working Group 3)

title: Early Career Working Group
description: Supports the advancement and success of CIROH's early career scientists by providing recommendations to CIROH leadership, informing early career scientist development strategy, and leading the organization of signature activities geared towards this community.

objectives: Support the development and implementation of a CIROH early career peer mentoring program.
Develop signature activities for CIROH's early career scientists to be delivered during DevCon, Science Meeting, and national conferences.
Identify resources that are available to and/or needed by CIROH early career scientists.

title: Community Resources Working Group
description: Strengthens CIROH’s digital infrastructure through modern DevOps practices, keeping platforms and tools reliable, scalable, and secure. Supports the community around R2OHC cyberinfrastructure, NGIAB, Research Datastream (NRDS), and other open-source repositories, and shares documentation, trainings, and news.
leads: Arpita Patel, The University of Alabama

objectives: Provide inputs for the CIROH cyberinfrastructure roadmaps to meet community and research needs, governance documents, cybersecurity protocols, and documentation for products/tools developed/deployed using CIROH IT.

Plan and develop the roadmap for community open source projects, develop governance and a PR review process, and implement CI/CD pipelines, automated tests and monitoring frameworks to accelerate deployment cycles.
Establish community contribution guidelines for documentation on CIROH Hub and governance, and help the community adopt IT and DevOps tools and processes.
Provide technical assistance and training sessions, and collaboratively develop articles/publications/presentations.
accomplishments: Held monthly virtual meetings.
Integrated 10+ models into NextGen In A Box (NGIAB) (Objective #2).
Expanded research datastream configurations using NGIAB to 6 active datastreams.
Supported extensive cloud and HPC usage, recording 76 users on AWS, 95 on GCP + 2i2c, 71 on Pantarhei + Wukong, and 141 on NSF ACCESS (Objective #1).
Merged the DocuHub and Portal repositories and deployed the CIROH Hub in March 2026 with new apps, documents and improved accessibility. Helped drive the total number of blogs to 30 (Objective #2).

CIROH Hub serves as the centralized place for CIROH resources, totaling 36 applications, 45 datasets, 271 publications, 40 presentations, 7 notebooks, and 19 courses as of September 2026 (Objective #2).
Three papers from research projects (NGIAB, CCNH and NRDS (in review)) published by working group members (Objective #4).
Two presentations by group members about research projects (CCNH, NRDS) (Objective #4).
Identified six training workshops for the Community NextGen track in the 2026 CIROH Developers Conference (Objective #4).

title: Artificial Intelligence Working Group
description: Informs the creation of CIROH's AI strategy and implementation roadmap. Encourages and supports white papers, facilitates DevCon AI/ML track workshops, synthesizes CIROH's AI research advances, and organizes activities to advance the state of CIROH's AI research.
leads: Jonathan Frame, The University of Alabama

objectives: Develop CIROH AI Strategy document (submit for CIROH Internal Review in Early December, NOAA Review in Early January, release at CIROH Developer's Conference).
Support and facilitate white papers that make progress towards CIROH's AI Strategy.
Organize AI/ML Track for CIROH Developer's Conference.

title: Evaluation and Testbeds Working Group
description: Clarifies what evaluation information is needed to support R2O and other uses of model and forecast evaluation, and promotes and improves the existing protocols, benchmark datasets, tools, and operational testbeds associated with evaluation.

objectives: Clarify evaluation information needed to support R2O.
Work with the CIROH R2O team and OWP management to clarify what evaluation evidence will help inform decisions about whether new approaches should be moved into operations
Define a complete suite of evaluation-related information that would support R2O decisions
Produce a template or example “pitch deck” for summarizing results for management using at least one newly developed method
Clarify, promote, and improve evaluation protocols, baseline datasets, evaluation tools, and operational testbeds.

Define the evaluation components and how they fit together—i.e., evaluation protocols (how to compare a new method), benchmark datasets (what to compare against), evaluation tools and metrics (e.g., TEEHR, FIMeval), operational testbeds (e.g., NRDS, CHPS in the cloud), and results communication
Map what exists: Document what is already available for each evaluation component, who maintains it, and where to find it
Raise awareness and support use: Raise awareness through speaker demos, and provide worked examples or quick-start guidance so researchers can apply each component
Collect feedback: Gather user feedback on barriers, usability, and gaps for each component

Prioritize improvements: Identify and prioritize improvements for future CIROH development (e.g., expanding protocols, collecting/developing new baseline datasets, improving tool usability, improving operational testbed integration)
Maintain the guidance: Maintain the Evaluation Guidance document as a living resource with a clear update process
Build community knowledge of evaluation approaches, applications, and testbeds.
Hold a monthly speaker series focused on evaluation and testbed-related topics. Record and share the sessions, with short summaries of key takeaways.
Use speaker input to shape guidance updates, evaluation improvements, and the R2O process
